bull.b: Extremely low leverage preserves financial flexibility while Oruka funds clinical development. With debt small relative to equity, the company faces less interest burden and refinancing pressure, leaving more capacity to direct capital toward its antibody pipeline and future growth opportunities.

The sharply larger asset base indicates a materially strengthened capital position compared with the prior annual period. That provides a more substantial financial foundation for ongoing research and clinical programs, although its ultimate durability depends on how efficiently Oruka converts capital into development progress.

Adding a commercial leader with experience at Arcutis, Incyte, UCB, AbbVie and TAP strengthens capabilities beyond research and development. This is a structural investment in potential launch readiness, market access and commercialization planning for dermatology and immunology biologic candidates.

bear.b: Oruka has not yet demonstrated product revenue, so its business model remains dependent on advancing clinical candidates toward approval and eventual commercialization. Until that transition occurs, the company lacks recurring operating inflows to offset research, development and corporate expenses.

Losses are expanding as Oruka increases spending ahead of commercialization, placing sustained pressure on earnings and capital efficiency. Persistent operating losses can reduce financial flexibility over time and make successful clinical execution and eventual revenue generation increasingly important to the investment case.

The worsening free-cash-flow trend shows that development spending is consuming cash at an increasing rate. Unless revenue or partnering inflows emerge, continued investment in the pipeline will require the company to rely more heavily on its existing capital base or future funding.
